Password breach screening has sampled unavailability
Keel This is network-shared screening transport evidence, not proof that a particular site’s last password was checked.

A sampled fresh lookup was skipped or could not complete: the shared lookup slots were busy. The sample was recorded 5 minutes ago. Samples are rate-limited, not counts of all skipped or failed checks.

No validated live response is recorded. Cached or locally filtered verdicts do not establish live service recovery.

Cached checks may still work when a fresh lookup cannot run. An unknown breach verdict does not block a password change; the other password rules and their role exemptions still apply. This evidence does not establish that all passwords set after a failure went unchecked.

Password breach-screening coverage is unknown
Keel Screening is configured, but its coverage for a particular password is unknown. Transport evidence is shared across the network; a network manager can review it. Cached checks may still work when a fresh lookup cannot run.
